Research question: can a lexicographic BFS (LexBFS) ordering be maintained
under edge insertions and deletions? No efficient fully dynamic algorithm is
known - this is an open problem.

The graph is undirected. The maintained result is any valid LexBFS ordering
(no fixed tie-break, any start vertex). Validity is certified by the (LB)
4-point property of Corneil and Krueger: for all positions a < b < c with
ac in E and ab not in E, there exists d < a with db in E and dc not in E.

Known territory: the static partition-refinement LexBFS of Habib, McConnell,
Paul and Viennot runs in O(n+m). Maintaining the refinement under updates is
the open part; partition-refinement structures are the natural toolbox.

Interface reminder: implement init(graph), insert_edge(graph, edge, state),
delete_edge(graph, edge, state). The state is passed in and returned; keep no
globals. Graphs are 0/1 adjacency matrices, vertex ids 0-based.

This is the open tier: a correct solution would be a research contribution in
its own right, so favour novel data structures over recomputation.

a full O(n^2) partition-refinement LexBFS recompute (always correct).

The (LB) 4-point property (Corneil & Krueger): for all positions a < b < c
with ac in E and ab not in E, there exists d < a with db in E and dc not in E.
"""

        return [0]

    # P: list of buckets (lists of vertices), in current order.
    # Q: FIFO queue of bucket references to refine.

    # vertex v, append v to order, refine all other buckets by v.

    Q = [P[0]]

        head += 1

        pu = o.index(u)
        candidates.append(o[:pu] + [v] + o[pu:])
    # Move u to end

        candidates.append(order[:pos[u]] + order[pos[u] + 1:] + [u])
    # Move u to beginning

def _lexbfs_full(graph):
    """Full partition-refinement LexBFS. Returns ordering list.

    Correct HMPV partition-refinement:
    - P: list of buckets (lists of vertices), in current order.
    - Q: FIFO queue of bucket references to refine.
    - Invariant: every non-empty bucket in P appears in Q exactly once.
    - At each step: pop front non-empty bucket from Q, take its first
      vertex v, append v to order, refine all OTHER buckets by v.
    - The surviving bucket b (if still non-empty) is re-inserted at the
      FRONT of P and re-enqueued first in Q, so its next vertex is
      processed before any vertex from a split bucket.
    """
    n = len(graph)
    if n == 0:
        return []
    if n == 1:
        return [0]

    Q = [P[0]]
    head = 0
    order = []

    while head < len(Q):
        b = Q[head]
        head += 1
        if not b:

        v = b.pop(0)

        # The surviving bucket b is re-enqueued first so that its next
        # vertex is processed before any vertex from a split bucket

        if b:
